flags.text: The ratchet skips any .ci file whose value is not a bare integer (read_int requires ^[0-9]+$), and .ci/min_coverage_views.txt holds 43.5 (raised 42.0 -> 43.5 in a0a230f). The views-coverage floor is therefore never compared: it can be lowered to any value with no budget-raise-ok trailer and the gate prints clean. units.key: § Emuqu — Build-Time Governance of a Consumer Physiology Score > 3. Methods > 3.1 Scoring-constants hash and version lock > 3.1.1 Hash and version lock
units.does: Specifies check_scoring_governance.sh: hash files Constants+RecoveryScore.swift then HRVThresholds.swift (missing -> exit 2), strip // comments, regex-extract static let numeric literals, sort per file, SHA-256 over 'path:symbol=value\n', first 16 hex; read ScoringVersion.current; baseline '<version> <hash>' (v3.1.oct2026 541b56e600080795); violation iff hash differs and version equals recorded version -> exit 1. Verified: recomputation gives 155 constants and 541b56e600080795; script logic matches. Both files contain only bare-literal static lets. Gaps: version-bump without baseline refresh leaves the gate open; missing version file / malformed baseline exit 1 not 2.
calls: .github/workflows/gates.yml::step script-gates/Copy perimeter, science register, scoring governance

flags.text: The lock compares only against the recorded (version, hash) line, and the gate passes whenever version != recorded_version. A maintainer who bumps ScoringVersion.current but does not rewrite .ci/scoring_constants_hash.txt leaves the gate permanently open: every later constant change under the new version also passes, because the recorded version still differs. Nothing forces the baseline to be refreshed, so 'a change to a constant forces a version change' (Sections 3.8/N1) holds only for the first change after each baseline update.

Paper step 7/Appendix A say the gate exits 2 when the version cannot be read and 2 for configuration errors. A missing ScoringVersion.swift raises an uncaught FileNotFoundError (Python exit 1, i.e. reported as a violation), and a baseline file without exactly two whitespace-separated tokens raises ValueError (exit 1).

The baseline line is rewritten by hand and nothing audits that edit: .ci/scoring_constants_hash.txt is not an integer so the monotonicity ratchet ignores it, and the gate only compares against whatever line is committed. History shows it: commit 14ecd58 (2026-10-06) changed Constants+RecoveryScore.swift (removed severeStrainThreshold, renamed moderateStrainThreshold) and rewrote the hash b81e8c3b2a364000 -> 541b56e600080795 under the unchanged version v3.1.oct2026, which is exactly 'digest moves while the version stays the same' passing CI.

Step 3 says a declaration whose right-hand side is not a bare numeric literal is not matched. CONST_RE only anchors the start of the value (`=\s*([-\d.]+)`), so an expression such as `= 60 * 0.5` or `= -someConst` is matched and only its leading literal (or a lone '-') is hashed; changing the rest of the expression would not move the hash. All 155 current declarations are bare literals, so this is latent.

units.key: § Emuqu — Build-Time Governance of a Consumer Physiology Score > 3. Methods > 3.4 Gates that test the gates > 3.4.1 Goes red: planted violations
units.does: Specifies verify_gates_fail.sh: per plant (name, gate, file, python mutation) skip on filter mismatch, SKIP if gate already red, backup, SKIP+restore if mutation fails, rerun gate, restore, nonzero=PASS else FAIL; 64 plants; then every check_*/enforce_* except check_gate_preflight.sh and NEEDS_BUILD (check_coverage.sh, check_thread_sanitizer.sh) must have its filename in the harness source, else exit 1; exit 1 on any FAIL, SKIP does not fail. Matches script (check() at :61, NEEDS_BUILD :550-553, grep at :565). The filename-presence check is satisfied by any mention including comments/echo text.

flags.text: The every-gate-has-a-plant check is `grep -q "$base" "$0"` over the harness's whole source, so a gate filename mentioned only in a comment or echo string counts as planted; the check proves a filename is mentioned, not that a plant exists.

The orphan_swift plant creates Emuqu/Sources/Utilities/PlantedOrphan.swift, which restore_all cannot remove (it only restores backed-up files); the file stays in the tree for every later plant and is deleted only at the very end (line 580). If the run is killed, or the unplanted-gate meta-check exits 1 (line 577) first, the planted file is left in Emuqu/Sources, and check_no_leaked_mutations.sh (which only parses verify_tests_fail.sh) does not detect it.

units.key: § Emuqu — Build-Time Governance of a Consumer Physiology Score > 3. Methods > 3.4 Gates that test the gates > 3.4.2 Fails closed: temp-file preflight
units.does: Specifies lib/preflight.sh helpers (gate_mktemp explicit template, exit 70 on failure/unwritable; gate_mktemp_dir 'same for directories'; gate_require_nonempty exit 70) and check_gate_preflight.sh scanning every scripts/*.sh except itself for bare mktemp, gate_mktemp without '|| exit' on the same line, and unresolved `source "$(dirname "$0")/..."`; 53 scripts, 10 guarded uses. Verified 53/10 by recomputation; gate logic matches. gate_mktemp_dir uses `mktemp -d -t label`, which fails on GNU.

flags.text: Paper says gate_mktemp uses an explicit template that behaves the same under BSD and GNU mktemp and that gate_mktemp_dir 'does the same for directories'. gate_mktemp_dir actually calls `mktemp -d -t "$label"`, the exact BSD-only form the gate_mktemp comment warns against: on GNU coreutils it fails ('too few X's in template'), so verify_gates_fail.sh and verify_tests_fail.sh exit 70 at startup on Linux. It fails closed, but both harnesses are unrunnable off macOS for a reason the paper does not state.

verify_gates_fail.sh takes the tree lock (line 37) before creating BACKUP_DIR with gate_mktemp_dir (line 38) and before installing the EXIT trap (line 39). Where gate_mktemp_dir fails (always on GNU mktemp, which rejects `-d -t label`), the script exits 70 with the lock directory left under .git holding a dead PID; every later mutator and simulate_ci.sh then prints 'stale lock ... that run never restored', a false leak warning.

units.key: § Emuqu — Build-Time Governance of a Consumer Physiology Score > 3. Methods > 3.5 Tests that must catch defects > 3.5.1 Targeted test mutations
units.does: Specifies verify_tests_fail.sh: 125 curated mutations each naming a suite; run suite alone with -only-testing and parallel testing off; classify 0 pass/1 fail/2 build-or-runner failure (banner or no 'Test Suite'/'Test Case'); retry baseline once on 2; SKIP if baseline not 0 or mutation not applicable; PASS if mutated run nonzero (including 2 = build failure of the mutated tree); any FAIL or SKIP exits 1; not in make ci or any workflow. Verified: 125 `mutate "` cases; run_suite uses -only-testing and -parallel-testing-enabled NO; exit 1 when FAIL or SKIP nonzero; no Makefile/workflow reference.

flags.text: Paper says 'Classifying build failures separately stops a broken build from counting as a catch'. The classification is only used for the baseline run; the mutated run is scored `code != 0 -> PASS`, so a mutation that fails to compile, or a transient build/runner failure (return 2) during the mutated run, is reported as 'caught'. A mutation whose replacement text does not compile proves nothing about the suite yet counts as PASS.

units.key: § Emuqu — Build-Time Governance of a Consumer Physiology Score > 3. Methods > 3.5 Tests that must catch defects > 3.5.2 Leaked-mutation detection and the tree lock
units.does: Specifies check_no_leaked_mutations.sh (split on '\nmutate "', target = first quoted Emuqu/...swift, original from o='...';assert or s.count('...') followed by comparator, unescape, resolve chr(N) concatenations, unparsed or leaked -> exit 1; runs on push/PR via gates.yml) and the tree lock in lib/preflight.sh (mkdir lock under git dir, owner+pid, live pid -> exit 75, dead -> warn and take over; reader gate_require_unmutated_tree used by simulate_ci.sh). Matches code (lock path from `git rev-parse --git-dir`, simulate_ci.sh:47). Leak check only detects mutations that remove the original text.

flags.text: Lock takeover reads the holder's pid file; between a holder's mkdir and its write of pid, a second mutator reads pid 0, treats the lock as stale, deletes it and takes it, so two mutators can run concurrently. The 'atomic mkdir' claim covers creation only.

The reader side has the same window as the takeover race: gate_require_unmutated_tree treats a lock with no pid file yet (pid read as 0) as stale and rm -rf's it, so a simulate_ci.sh run that starts between a mutator's mkdir and its pid write deletes the live mutator's lock and proceeds to measure a tree that is about to be mutated.

units.key: § Emuqu — Build-Time Governance of a Consumer Physiology Score > 3. Methods > 3.6 One-way budget ratchets > 3.6.2 Monotonicity gate
units.does: Specifies check_budget_monotonicity.sh: baseline from arg, origin/$GITHUB_BASE_REF, BUDGET_BASE_REF, else none; none/all-zero/unresolvable -> exit 1 if BUDGET_REQUIRE_BASELINE else skip exit 0; trailers '^budget-raise-ok:' case-insensitive from baseline..HEAD; per .ci/*.txt sorted: skip non-integer current, absent or non-integer baseline; min_* floors loosen on decrease, others on increase; acknowledged loosening ALLOWED else violation -> exit 1. CI wiring: ci.yml uses input or HEAD~1, root commit with .ci edits compares to HEAD, sets require; gates.yml passes origin/base on PR (no require flag) and HEAD~1 with require on push. Matches code; push path only compares the last commit; the non-integer files (.ci/min_coverage_views.txt = 43.5 and .ci/scoring_constants_hash.txt) are never compared.

flags.text: On push to main the per-push workflow compares budgets only against HEAD~1 of the pushed head. A push of several commits in which an earlier commit raises a budget (and the last does not touch it) is never compared against the pre-push state, so the loosening passes with no budget-raise-ok trailer. 'A push to main therefore cannot skip the comparison' is true only for single-commit pushes.

The ratchet skips any .ci file whose value is not a bare integer (read_int requires ^[0-9]+$), and .ci/min_coverage_views.txt holds 43.5 (raised 42.0 -> 43.5 in a0a230f). The views-coverage floor is therefore never compared: it can be lowered to any value with no budget-raise-ok trailer and the gate prints clean. Contradicts 'Each CI budget file may move only in the tightening direction its filename declares' and README's 'Fails any diff that raises/loosens a value in .ci/*.txt'; check_coverage.sh enforces whatever value is committed.

Deleting .ci/min_coverage.txt, min_coverage_logic.txt or min_coverage_views.txt is not seen by the ratchet (it only iterates files present in the tree) and check_coverage.sh silently falls back to hard-coded floors 16/30/0 instead of the committed 44/45/43.5, so the coverage floors can be dropped with no trailer and no failure.

flags.text: Lock takeover reads the holder's pid file; between a holder's mkdir and its write of pid, a second mutator reads pid 0, treats the lock as stale, deletes it and takes it, so two mutators can run concurrently. The 'atomic mkdir' claim covers creation only.
